snippets.headline: Glycemic Status Assessment measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had an A1c test during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets GSD when they have an A1c test in the measurement year, represented in patient detail by `gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` at the grouping grain. For the governed overall rate, query `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`.

snippets.headline: GSD measures whether diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 received an A1c test during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment. Its eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires an A1c test in the measurement year. Retrieve the rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level evidence or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` instead of the metric view.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control rates measure results among tested patients, while Glycemic Status compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For GSD, good and poor glycemic control rates are computed only among A1c-tested patients, not all eligible diabetic patients. The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. The poor control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, using the same tested-patient denominator. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control bands combine A1c testing status with good, moderate, and poor result categories.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Use the derived GSD glycemic control band expression to classify A1c testing and control outcomes. The exact expression is `CASE WHEN NOT gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag THEN 'Not tested' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8 THEN 'Good (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9 THEN 'Poor (>9%)' ELSE 'Moderate (8-9%)' END`. The complete output value list is `Not tested`, `Good (<8%)`, `Poor (>9%)`, and `Moderate (8-9%)`. This band combines the testing status and A1c result category, so `Not tested` is a testing gap rather than a clinical control range.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level Glycemic Status reporting combines eligible counts, testing compliance, control rates, and average latest A1c.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level GSD reporting, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` directly because `clinic_id` is present on the GSD patient-level table. The curated clinic query groups by `clinic_id` and computes `COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients`, `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`, and `AVG(evidence_value) AS avg_latest_a1c`. Here the GSD compliance denominator is all eligible patients in that clinic, while good and poor control denominators are only patients with `numerator_flag`. This pattern is the source for clinic-level A1c testing and control comparison.

snippets.headline: Average latest A1c summarizes recorded A1c values and is separate from testing compliance and control rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The average latest A1c percentage among tested patients is represented by `AVG(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value)`. In clinic-level GSD reporting, this appears alongside `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, and `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`. The numerator for the average is the A1c evidence value, and the intended denominator is the count of rows with non-null `evidence_value` included by `AVG`. Use this only for A1c-tested evidence analysis; it is not a compliance rate.

snippets.headline: Measure rates come from governed metric views, while patient detail and care gap lists come from gold adherence tables.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For measure rates, use the matching metric view and query the governed metric with `MEASURE(...)`: `gsd_compliance_metrics`, `ked_compliance_metrics`, `bpd_compliance_metrics`, `spd_compliance_metrics`, or `eed_compliance_metrics`. The instruction says never to `SUM` or `AVG` a rate column, because rates are governed measures rather than additive facts. For patient-level detail, evidence fields, care gap lists, and custom clinic or panel breakdowns, use the corresponding `gold_adherence_<measure>` table. In the patient-level tables, `status = 'NOT_MET'` means a care gap and `status = 'MET'` means compliant.

snippets.headline: Metric views answer rate questions, while gold adherence tables answer patient-level evidence and care-gap questions.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Each measure has two complementary sources: a compliance metric view for rates and a `gold_adherence_<measure>` table for patient-level detail plus evidence. Use `gsd_compliance_metrics`, `ked_compliance_metrics`, `bpd_compliance_metrics`, `spd_compliance_metrics`, or `eed_compliance_metrics` for governed rates. Use the corresponding `gold_adherence_gsd`, `gold_adherence_ked`, `gold_adherence_bpd`, `gold_adherence_spd`, or `gold_adherence_eed` table when the question asks which patients met a measure, what evidence supports it, or where care gaps exist.

snippets.headline: A care gap is a patient-level record marked not met, while met records represent compliant patients.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: In every patient-level gold adherence table, `status = 'NOT_MET'` means the patient has a care gap and `status = 'MET'` means the patient is compliant. To count KED care gaps, use the exact governed query `SELECT COUNT(*) AS ked_care_gaps FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked WHERE status = 'NOT_MET'`. The same status interpretation applies to the corresponding gold adherence tables for GSD, BPD, SPD, and EED.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level comparisons across diabetes measures use Glycemic Status attribution and report each measure’s eligible clinic-attributed patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level comparisons across all five diabetes measures, the curated pattern uses GSD as the clinic attribution source. The union labels the complete measure set as `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`, each carrying `measurement_year`, `clinic_id`, and `numerator_flag`; KED, BPD, SPD, and EED are joined to the GSD clinic CTE by `patient_id` and `measurement_year`. The clinic rates are `COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>' AND numerator_flag) / COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>')` for each measure. Because the KED branch uses an inner join to GSD, clinic-level KED rates represent clinic-attributed KED patients rather than all KED-eligible patients aged 18-85.

snippets.headline: Age-band reporting for Glycemic Status, Blood Pressure control, and Eye Exam uses three shared adult bands.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The GSD age band logic, which also matches the GSD/BPD/EED metric views, is `CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75' END`. The complete output value list is `18-44`, `45-64`, and `65-75`. Use these exact cut points and labels for GSD, BPD, and EED age-band reporting to match the metric views. The upper band label reflects the 18-75 eligible age range for those measures.

snippets.headline: Eye Exam patients use Glycemic Status rows for clinic and panel attribution when reporting clinic-level rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Attach clinic or panel attribution to EED patients by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` on `gold_adherence_eed.patient_id = gold_adherence_gsd.patient_id AND gold_adherence_eed.measurement_year = gold_adherence_gsd.measurement_year`. The curated relationship is many-to-one from EED to GSD, and every EED patient has a GSD row. Use this join to bring `clinic_id` and `panel_id` onto EED rows for clinic or panel breakdowns. A verified sample computes clinic EED rate as `COUNT_IF(e.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)` after this join and groups by `g.clinic_id`.

snippets.headline: Care gap lists include only non-compliant patient rows, while compliant rows represent completed measure requirements.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The universal care gap filter in the gold adherence tables is to INCLUDE rows where `status = 'NOT_MET'`. The corresponding compliant status is `status = 'MET'`, so do not infer care gaps from the absence of evidence fields alone unless a measure-specific snippet says so. This applies to all five patient-level tables: `gold_adherence_gsd`, `gold_adherence_ked`, `gold_adherence_bpd`, `gold_adherence_spd`, and `gold_adherence_eed`. Standard care gap counts use `COUNT_IF(<table>.status = 'NOT_MET')` or `WHERE <table>.status = 'NOT_MET'`.

snippets.headline: SPD measures statin therapy among diabetic adults aged 40 through 75 who were dispensed a statin during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: SPD means Statin Therapy. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 40-75, and compliance requires statin dispensing in the measurement year. Retrieve the governed rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`SPD Compliance Rate`) AS spd_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.spd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level detail or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`.

snippets.headline: A patient’s diabetes gap burden counts open gaps across the five measures after applying the non-compliant status rule.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: A patient's number of open diabetes care gaps is computed by unioning gap rows from all five gold adherence tables and counting rows per `patient_id`. The standard gap inclusion rule in each branch is exactly `status = 'NOT_MET'` for `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`; the complete measure label list is `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`. The instruction query uses `UNION ALL`, then `SELECT patient_id, COUNT(*) AS gap_count FROM gaps GROUP BY patient_id`, and finally counts patients by `gap_count`. Because the query groups only by `patient_id`, keep the same measurement-year scope upstream if multiple years are present and a per-year gap burden is needed.

snippets.headline: Each KED eGFR value-set version connects to observed patients through matching LOINC codes in the clinical observation records.
snippets.source: Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment
snippets.content: The complete relationship path for eGFR code matching is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` filtered by `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'` -> `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment.code` equals `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.loinc_code` -> observation patients via `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.patient_id`. snippets.headline: Care gap lists include only non-compliant patient rows, while compliant rows represent completed measure requirements.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The universal care gap filter in the gold adherence tables is to INCLUDE rows where `status = 'NOT_MET'`. The corresponding compliant status is `status = 'MET'`, so do not infer care gaps from the absence of evidence fields alone unless a measure-specific snippet says so. This applies to all five patient-level tables: `gold_adherence_gsd`, `gold_adherence_ked`, `gold_adherence_bpd`, `gold_adherence_spd`, and `gold_adherence_eed`. Standard care gap counts use `COUNT_IF(<table>.status = 'NOT_MET')` or `WHERE <table>.status = 'NOT_MET'`.

snippets.headline: A care gap is a patient-level record marked not met, while met records represent compliant patients.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: In every patient-level gold adherence table, `status = 'NOT_MET'` means the patient has a care gap and `status = 'MET'` means the patient is compliant. To count KED care gaps, use the exact governed query `SELECT COUNT(*) AS ked_care_gaps FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked WHERE status = 'NOT_MET'`. The same status interpretation applies to the corresponding gold adherence tables for GSD, BPD, SPD, and EED.

snippets.headline: A patient’s diabetes gap burden counts open gaps across the five measures after applying the non-compliant status rule.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: A patient's number of open diabetes care gaps is computed by unioning gap rows from all five gold adherence tables and counting rows per `patient_id`. The standard gap inclusion rule in each branch is exactly `status = 'NOT_MET'` for `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`; the complete measure label list is `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`. The instruction query uses `UNION ALL`, then `SELECT patient_id, COUNT(*) AS gap_count FROM gaps GROUP BY patient_id`, and finally counts patients by `gap_count`. Because the query groups only by `patient_id`, keep the same measurement-year scope upstream if multiple years are present and a per-year gap burden is needed.

snippets.headline: Blood Pressure control gaps include both missing readings and uncontrolled latest readings, which support separate outreach lists.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD care gaps split into no-reading gaps and uncontrolled latest-reading gaps. INCLUDE all BPD gap list/count rows with `gold_adherence_bpd.status = 'NOT_MET'`, which covers uncontrolled blood pressure OR no reading. INCLUDE uncontrolled latest-reading gaps and EXCLUDE no-reading gaps with `gold_adherence_bpd.status = 'NOT_MET' AND gold_adherence_bpd.bp_datetime IS NOT NULL`. INCLUDE patients with no BP reading in the measurement year with `gold_adherence_bpd.bp_datetime IS NULL`.

snippets.headline: Measure rates come from governed metric views, while patient detail and care gap lists come from gold adherence tables.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For measure rates, use the matching metric view and query the governed metric with `MEASURE(...)`: `gsd_compliance_metrics`, `ked_compliance_metrics`, `bpd_compliance_metrics`, `spd_compliance_metrics`, or `eed_compliance_metrics`. The instruction says never to `SUM` or `AVG` a rate column, because rates are governed measures rather than additive facts. For patient-level detail, evidence fields, care gap lists, and custom clinic or panel breakdowns, use the corresponding `gold_adherence_<measure>` table. In the patient-level tables, `status = 'NOT_MET'` means a care gap and `status = 'MET'` means compliant.

snippets.headline: Kidney Evaluation outreach for closing uACR gaps targets patients who already completed eGFR but lack uACR.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)

INCLUDE those rows with `gold_adherence_ked.egfr_flag AND NOT gold_adherence_ked.uacr_flag`. This is distinct from the broad KED care gap filter `gold_adherence_ked.status = 'NOT_MET'`, which includes patients missing eGFR, missing uACR, or missing both. snippets.content: Among rows included with `status = 'NOT_MET'`, BPD is assigned the gap reason `'BP not controlled / no reading'`, SPD is assigned `'No statin dispensed'`, and EED is assigned `'No diabetic eye exam'`. These exact labels are counted from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`, and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed` using `COUNT(*)` grouped by measure and gap reason. ## 198 statin patients have a diagnosis the protocol lists as a statin contraindication

**198 patients** have at least one statin order and also have a diagnosis of their own that falls under a statin contraindication in the care protocol. That's about 4% of the **4,741 patients with any statin order**. All 198 match on **pregnancy**. None match on hepatic disease. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2f22634f491243c9b02e532c0bd0fdf0?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_f7ad4f)

### The protocol rules

The protocol (section "CP sec4") has two statin contraindication rules, each defined by a set of diagnosis codes:

<!-- begin-embedded:query_76fb61 -->
| subject | predicate | object | source | icd10_codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DRUGCLASS-STATIN | contraindicatedWith | CONTRA_HEPATIC | CP sec4 | K74, K70 |
| DRUGCLASS-STATIN | contraindicatedWith | CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O26, Z34, O15, O00 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_76fb61 -->

The pregnancy matches are almost all **Z34.90 "Normal pregnancy"**. A few patients also have eclampsia (O15.9) or tubal pregnancy (O00.1). [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2f22634f491243c9b02e532c0bd0fdf0?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_0dd347)

### How I matched them

I used the same steps as the earlier single-patient check, run for every patient: [Single-patient statin contraindication path](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/c43f1f5fe49540b2b5882db237244ce4?o=7474653847172668)

1. Find each patient's medication orders that roll up to the statin drug class.
2. Look up the statin contraindication rules in the protocol.
3. Get the diagnosis codes in each rule's code set.
4. Match the patient's own encounter diagnoses, including more specific codes under each listed code. [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Most matches don't line up in time with the statin

The protocol rule only lists codes. It has no time window, so 198 is the count for any pregnancy diagnosis ever recorded. Narrower readings give smaller counts:

| Definition | Patients |
|---|---|
| Pregnancy diagnosis at any time (protocol as written) | **198** |
| Diagnosis recorded on or after the patient's first statin order | 94 |
| Diagnosis recorded within the statin order period, or in the 280 days before it (my estimate of a full pregnancy) | 80 |

[Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2f22634f491243c9b02e532c0bd0fdf0?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_f7ad4f)

Many patients' pregnancy diagnoses come years before their first statin order. For example, one patient was pregnant in 2017 and started simvastatin in 2020. Those matches are historical, not active conflicts. The earlier single-patient review reached the same conclusion. [Single-patient statin contraindication path](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/c43f1f5fe49540b2b5882db237244ce4?o=7474653847172668) The **80 patients** whose pregnancy falls during or close to their statin order period are the best list to review clinically.

### Caveats
- "Prescribed a statin" here means any statin order ever placed. It doesn't mean the order was active or that the statin was dispensed in 2025.
- The data has no pregnancy end dates, so the time-based counts are estimates.
- This is synthetic demo data aligned to HEDIS, not certified by NCQA. The SPD measure tables don't apply these contraindication exclusions.

WITH rx AS (
  SELECT m.`patient_id`, MIN(m.`start_ts`) AS first_statin_ts, MAX(m.`start_ts`) AS last_statin_ts, concat_ws('; ', collect_set(m.`description`)) AS statins
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_order_med` m
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`rxnorm_closure` cls ON m.`rxnorm_code` = cls.`descendant_code` AND cls.`ancestor_code` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
  GROUP BY m.`patient_id`
),
rule AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT `object`, `source` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges`
  WHERE `subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND `predicate` = 'contraindicatedWith'
),
vs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT `segment_id`, `code` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` WHERE `code_system` = 'ICD10CM'
),
dx AS (
  SELECT d.`patient_id`, d.`icd10_code`, d.`description`, d.`onset_date`, c.`ancestor_code`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_pat_enc_dx` d
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` c ON d.`icd10_code` = c.`descendant_code`
),
hits AS (
  SELECT rx.`patient_id`, rule.`object` AS contraindication, rule.`source`, dx.`icd10_code`, dx.`description`, dx.`onset_date`, rx.first_statin_ts, rx.statins
  FROM rx CROSS JOIN rule
  JOIN vs ON vs.`segment_id` = rule.`object`
  JOIN dx ON dx.`ancestor_code` = vs.`code` AND dx.`patient_id` = rx.`patient_id`
)
SELECT `patient_id`, concat_ws(', ', collect_set(contraindication)) AS contraindications, first(`source`) AS protocol_source,
  concat_ws('; ', collect_set(concat(`icd10_code`, ' ', `description`))) AS diagnoses,
  MIN(`onset_date`) AS first_dx_onset, MAX(`onset_date`) AS last_dx_onset, MIN(first_statin_ts) AS first_statin_order, first(statins) AS statins
FROM hits GROUP BY `patient_id` ORDER BY `patient_id`

SELECT e.`subject`, e.`predicate`, e.`object`, e.`source`, concat_ws(', ', collect_set(v.`code`)) AS icd10_codes
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` e
LEFT JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` v ON v.`segment_id` = e.`object` AND v.`code_system` = 'ICD10CM'
WHERE e.`subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND e.`predicate` LIKE 'contraindicated%'
GROUP BY ALL

WITH rx_orders AS (
  SELECT m.`patient_id`, m.`start_ts`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_order_med` m
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`rxnorm_closure` cls ON m.`rxnorm_code` = cls.`descendant_code` AND cls.`ancestor_code` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
),
rx AS (SELECT `patient_id`, MIN(`start_ts`) AS first_ts, MAX(`start_ts`) AS last_ts FROM rx_orders GROUP BY `patient_id`),
rule AS (SELECT DISTINCT `object` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` WHERE `subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND `predicate` = 'contraindicatedWith'),
vs AS (SELECT DISTINCT `segment_id`, `code` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` WHERE `code_system` = 'ICD10CM'),
hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.`patient_id`, rule.`object` AS contra, d.`onset_date`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_pat_enc_dx` d
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` c ON d.`icd10_code` = c.`descendant_code`
  JOIN vs ON vs.`code` = c.`ancestor_code`
  JOIN rule ON rule.`object` = vs.`segment_id`
  WHERE d.`patient_id` IN (SELECT `patient_id` FROM rx)
),
p AS (
  SELECT h.`patient_id`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN contra='CONTRA_PREGNANCY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) preg,
    MAX(CASE WHEN contra='CONTRA_HEPATIC' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) hep,
    MAX(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1) AND h.`onset_date` BETWEEN date_sub(CAST(rx.first_ts AS DATE), 280) AND CAST(rx.last_ts AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) overlap_statin_period,
    MAX(CASE WHEN h.`onset_date` >= CAST(rx.first_ts AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) dx_after_first_statin
  FROM hits h JOIN rx ON rx.`patient_id` = h.`patient_id` GROUP BY h.`patient_id`
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rx) AS patients_with_statin_order,
  COUNT(*) AS statin_pts_with_contraindicating_dx,
  SUM(preg) AS with_pregnancy_dx, SUM(hep) AS with_hepatic_dx, SUM(preg*hep) AS with_both,
  SUM(dx_after_first_statin) AS dx_onset_on_or_after_first_statin_order,
  SUM(overlap_statin_period) AS dx_within_statin_order_span_incl_280d_lookback
FROM p

snippets.headline: Average latest A1c summarizes recorded A1c values and is separate from testing compliance and control rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The average latest A1c percentage among tested patients is represented by `AVG(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value)`. In clinic-level GSD reporting, this appears alongside `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, and `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`. The numerator for the average is the A1c evidence value, and the intended denominator is the count of rows with non-null `evidence_value` included by `AVG`. Use this only for A1c-tested evidence analysis; it is not a compliance rate.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level Glycemic Status reporting combines eligible counts, testing compliance, control rates, and average latest A1c.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level GSD reporting, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` directly because `clinic_id` is present on the GSD patient-level table. The curated clinic query groups by `clinic_id` and computes `COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients`, `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`, and `AVG(evidence_value) AS avg_latest_a1c`. Here the GSD compliance denominator is all eligible patients in that clinic, while good and poor control denominators are only patients with `numerator_flag`. This pattern is the source for clinic-level A1c testing and control comparison.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control rates measure results among tested patients, while Glycemic Status compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For GSD, good and poor glycemic control rates are computed only among A1c-tested patients, not all eligible diabetic patients. The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. The poor control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, using the same tested-patient denominator. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

snippets.headline: Glycemic Status Assessment measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had an A1c test during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets GSD when they have an A1c test in the measurement year, represented in patient detail by `gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` at the grouping grain. For the governed overall rate, query `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control bands combine A1c testing status with good, moderate, and poor result categories.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Use the derived GSD glycemic control band expression to classify A1c testing and control outcomes. The exact expression is `CASE WHEN NOT gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag THEN 'Not tested' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8 THEN 'Good (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9 THEN 'Poor (>9%)' ELSE 'Moderate (8-9%)' END`. The complete output value list is `Not tested`, `Good (<8%)`, `Poor (>9%)`, and `Moderate (8-9%)`. This band combines the testing status and A1c result category, so `Not tested` is a testing gap rather than a clinical control range.

snippets.headline: GSD measures whether diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 received an A1c test during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment. Its eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires an A1c test in the measurement year. Retrieve the rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level evidence or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` instead of the metric view.

snippets.headline: Eye Exam patients use Glycemic Status rows for clinic and panel attribution when reporting clinic-level rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Attach clinic or panel attribution to EED patients by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` on `gold_adherence_eed.patient_id = gold_adherence_gsd.patient_id AND gold_adherence_eed.measurement_year = gold_adherence_gsd.measurement_year`. The curated relationship is many-to-one from EED to GSD, and every EED patient has a GSD row. Use this join to bring `clinic_id` and `panel_id` onto EED rows for clinic or panel breakdowns. A verified sample computes clinic EED rate as `COUNT_IF(e.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)` after this join and groups by `g.clinic_id`.

snippets.headline: Blood Pressure control measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a latest reading below 140 over 90.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD means Blood Pressure control for diabetic patients aged 18-75. ## Definition
HEDIS measure of kidney-health evaluation in patients with diabetes. Its numerator is **compound**: it requires two different lab tests in the same year.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **18–85** at the end of the measurement year.

* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_ked` (`egfr_flag`, `uacr_flag`)

pages_read.body:
**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure for assessing kidney
health in diabetic patients. Its numerator is **compound** — it requires two different tests in the same year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–85** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** **both** of the following in the measurement year:
  1. an **eGFR** (estimated glomerular filtration rate) test — value set `KED_EGFR`, and
  2. a **uACR** (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) test — value set `KED_UACR`.

A patient is **MET** only when **both** components are present; missing either is a care gap. Because the two
components are tracked separately, the **eGFR Test Rate** and **uACR Test Rate** are each exposed in
`ked_compliance_metrics` alongside the combined **KED Compliance Rate**. In this demo uACR is the limiting
component (eGFR ~92%, uACR ~51%, combined ~51%).

> The eGFR value set spans LOINC vintages (e.g. `33914-3` MDRD and `98979-8`) — a reminder that value sets
> evolve and a measure must accept all valid codes for the concept. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

## KED: who's eligible and what counts as compliant

**Eligible (denominator):** patients in the **Diabetes Cohort** (any ICD-10-CM diagnosis under E10, E11 or E13, child codes included) who are **18–85 years old on Dec 31 of the measurement year**. Each eligible patient has one row. [KED — Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/9edbb1f7-62bd-405e-9bb6-fa9413b7d243?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Diabetes Cohort](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/402e8af3-3e5a-4a46-aa36-22dcd8df5e64?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_ked?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

**Compliant (numerator):** the patient needs **both** of these tests in the same measurement year:
1. an **eGFR** test (value set `KED_EGFR`, LOINC 33914-3 MDRD or 98979-8 CKD-EPI), **and**
2. a **uACR** test (value set `KED_UACR`, e.g. 14959-1 microalbumin/creatinine ratio).

If either test is missing, the patient has a care gap. Doing only one of the two tests never counts as compliant. [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-d3494f59-4cda-47e7-babd-761d66786d55) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

The upper age limit is higher than for the related measures. GSD and eye exam stop at 75, and SPD covers ages 40–75, so patients aged 76–85 are in KED only. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-58db899b-2b13-4088-b3cf-5974272cc9a7)

## What this looks like in the current data
<!-- begin-embedded:query_a8d930 -->
| measurement_year | rows_ | patients | eligible | min_age | max_age | met_both | ked_rate | egfr_rate | uacr_rate | missing_both | missing_uacr_only | missing_egfr_only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026 | 2802 | 2802 | 2802 | 18 | 85 | 1327 | 0.4736 | 0.8754 | 0.4736 | 349 | 1126 | 0 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_a8d930 -->

- **2,802 eligible patients**, ages 18–85, measurement year 2026.
- **1,327 compliant (47.4%).** 87.5% had an eGFR test but only 47.4% had a uACR test. The overall rate equals the uACR rate, so **uACR is the bottleneck**.
- Of the 1,475 care gaps, **1,126 are missing only the uACR test** and 349 are missing both. No patient is missing only eGFR. Ordering uACR for patients who already had an eGFR is the biggest opportunity to close gaps.

## Changes since earlier analyses
- The KED table no longer has the `status`, `numerator_flag`, `egfr_flag` and `uacr_flag` columns. I counted a test as done when it has a result date in the year.
- The governed `ked_compliance_metrics` view could not be found, so the rates above come from the patient-level table, not the governed KED Compliance Rate.
- Earlier analyses covered only 2025. The table now holds **2026 only**. eGFR testing is still around 88%, so the expected 2026 drop in eGFR from the updated code list hasn't happened in this data.

*This is HEDIS-aligned demo data, not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD and frailty exclusions aren't applied, so the eligible count runs slightly high.*

## GSD poor-control rate: only A1c-tested patients, A1c above 9%

The poor-control rate only counts **patients who had an A1c test** in the measurement year, not every eligible patient. Poor control means a **latest A1c above 9%**. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-96a50ca6-4d7e-49f5-9be7-959c98fc976b) [GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/1045ab28-3390-4c2f-a056-381c1019c345?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

**How the GSD rates differ**

| Metric | Denominator | Numerator |
|---|---|---|
| GSD compliance rate | All eligible GSD patients (diabetes, age 18–75) | Patients with ≥1 A1c test in the year |
| Good-control rate | A1c-tested patients only | Latest A1c **< 8%** |
| Poor-control rate | A1c-tested patients only | Latest A1c **> 9%** |

[Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5a6324fb-8fbe-4a26-abd6-1a0ebcc5cd00) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-93568b56-c797-4116-8166-db6fa073557b)

**What this means in practice**
- A1c results are sorted into four groups: *Not tested*, *Good (<8%)*, *Moderate (8–9%)* and *Poor (>9%)*. "Not tested" is a testing gap, not a control level, so untested patients don't count toward the poor-control rate. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-d32dc0bb-67e2-402a-9aaf-ffe1f3a5ca0c)
- Because untested patients are left out, a clinic with low testing can still show a low poor-control rate. Always read the poor-control rate next to the compliance (testing) rate.
- This is different from a common outside definition of "poorly controlled diabetes," which counts all diabetic patients whose latest A1c is above 9%. There, untested patients usually count as poorly controlled. [Poorly controlled diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/89de86e4-4d18-4848-9c16-cfa8b107ba8b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- Separately, the step that flags patients for an A1c follow-up uses a lower cutoff: **A1c ≥ 7%**. Don't confuse it with the GSD poor-control cutoff. [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

These definitions are demo content modeled on HEDIS, not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD and frailty exclusions aren't applied, so the eligible-patient count runs slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-a5cf6b49-638b-4371-a06e-271d331c3089) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

snippets.headline: This agent covers five HEDIS-aligned diabetes quality measures, but its results are a demonstration rather than NCQA-certified reporting.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The agent answers questions about five HEDIS-aligned diabetes measures: GSD, KED, BPD, SPD, and EED. This is a HEDIS-aligned demo and is not NCQA-certified. The available data is organized into matching patient-level gold adherence tables and governed compliance metric views in the Care Protocol semantic layer.

snippets.headline: Eye Exam measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a retinal or diabetic eye exam during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: EED means Eye Exam for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets EED when they had a retinal or diabetic eye exam in the measurement year, represented by `gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level EED compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all EED-eligible rows at the grouping grain. Use `MEASURE(`EED Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.eed_compliance_metrics` for governed rate reporting.

snippets.headline: EED measures retinal or diabetic eye examination among diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: EED means Eye Exam. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires a retinal or diabetic eye exam in the measurement year. Retrieve the governed rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`EED Compliance Rate`) AS eed_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.eed_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level evidence or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed`.

snippets.headline: Diabetes quality reporting in this agent covers five HEDIS-aligned demo measures and is not NCQA-certified.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: This Genie Agent covers five diabetes quality measures: GSD, KED, BPD, SPD, and EED. The measures are described as HEDIS-aligned demo content and explicitly are not NCQA-certified. The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy, using diagnoses under `E10`, `E11`, and `E13`. Analysts should treat these rules as the measure universe for this semantic layer rather than as certified HEDIS specifications.

snippets.headline: Diabetes eligibility includes diagnoses subsumed under the E10, E11, and E13 ICD-10-CM hierarchy families.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy, specifically diagnoses under E10, E11, and E13. Use this governed cohort definition when interpreting any of the five measure populations. Do not infer diabetes eligibility from unrelated diagnosis codes or from measure status alone.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level comparisons across diabetes measures use Glycemic Status attribution and report each measure’s eligible clinic-attributed patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level comparisons across all five diabetes measures, the curated pattern uses GSD as the clinic attribution source. The union labels the complete measure set as `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`, each carrying `measurement_year`, `clinic_id`, and `numerator_flag`; KED, BPD, SPD, and EED are joined to the GSD clinic CTE by `patient_id` and `measurement_year`. The clinic rates are `COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>' AND numerator_flag) / COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>')` for each measure. Because the KED branch uses an inner join to GSD, clinic-level KED rates represent clinic-attributed KED patients rather than all KED-eligible patients aged 18-85.

snippets.headline: GSD measures whether diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 received an A1c test during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment. Its eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires an A1c test in the measurement year. Retrieve the rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level evidence or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` instead of the metric view.

snippets.headline: KED measures kidney evaluation for diabetic adults aged 18 through 85 who received both required laboratory tests.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED means Kidney Health Evaluation. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-85, and compliance requires both an eGFR test and a uACR test; uACR is usually the limiting component. Retrieve all three governed rates with `SELECT MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`) AS ked_rate, MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`) AS egfr_rate, MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`) AS uacr_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.ked_compliance_metrics`. Do not treat completion of only one component as KED compliance.

snippets.headline: A patient’s diabetes gap burden counts open gaps across the five measures after applying the non-compliant status rule.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: A patient's number of open diabetes care gaps is computed by unioning gap rows from all five gold adherence tables and counting rows per `patient_id`. The standard gap inclusion rule in each branch is exactly `status = 'NOT_MET'` for `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`; the complete measure label list is `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`. The instruction query uses `UNION ALL`, then `SELECT patient_id, COUNT(*) AS gap_count FROM gaps GROUP BY patient_id`, and finally counts patients by `gap_count`. Because the query groups only by `patient_id`, keep the same measurement-year scope upstream if multiple years are present and a per-year gap burden is needed.

snippets.headline: Governed metric views support standard rate reporting by year, status, age band, and measure dimensions.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Metric views expose dimensions for governed measure reporting: Measurement Year, Compliance Status, Age Band, and Measure. Use these dimensions when grouping governed measures, such as `SELECT `Age Band`, MEASURE(`SPD Compliance Rate`) AS spd_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.spd_compliance_metrics GROUP BY `Age Band` ORDER BY `Age Band``. The metric view should be preferred for standard rate questions like “overall GSD compliance rate” or “SPD rate by age band.” Use patient-level gold tables only when the question requires evidence fields, patient lists, or custom clinic/panel attribution.

snippets.headline: Glycemic Status Assessment measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had an A1c test during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets GSD when they have an A1c test in the measurement year, represented in patient detail by `gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` at the grouping grain. For the governed overall rate, query `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`.

snippets.headline: SPD measures statin therapy among diabetic adults aged 40 through 75 who were dispensed a statin during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: SPD means Statin Therapy. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 40-75, and compliance requires statin dispensing in the measurement year. Retrieve the governed rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`SPD Compliance Rate`) AS spd_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.spd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level detail or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`.

snippets.headline: Kidney Health Evaluation requires both kidney tests for eligible diabetic patients aged 18–85, with uACR usually limiting completion.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED means Kidney Health Evaluation for diabetic patients aged 18-85. A patient meets KED only when BOTH kidney tests are present: an eGFR test and a uACR test, represented by the KED numerator. The governed metric view supports `MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`)`, `MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`)`, and `MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`)`; use these measures from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.ked_compliance_metrics` when comparing KED overall compliance with the two components. The curated instruction notes that uACR is usually the limiting component, so questions about closing the KED gap often focus on missing uACR.

snippets.headline: Compliance rates must come from governed measure views rather than averaging or summing stored rate values.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For measure rates, query the matching compliance metric view with the governed `MEASURE()` expression; never `SUM` or `AVG` a rate column. The metric views expose rates with dimensions `Measurement Year`, `Compliance Status`, `Age Band`, and `Measure`. Use the exact measure expression corresponding to the requested measure, such as `MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`.

snippets.headline: BPD measures blood-pressure control among diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 using the most recent reading.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD means Blood Pressure control. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires that the most recent blood-pressure reading is `<140/90`. Retrieve the governed rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`BPD Compliance Rate`) AS bpd_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bpd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level detail or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd`.

snippets.headline: Blood Pressure control measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a latest reading below 140 over 90.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD means Blood Pressure control for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets BPD when their most recent blood pressure reading is controlled, defined in the instruction as `<140/90`. The standard patient-level BPD compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_bpd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all BPD-eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd` at the grouping grain. Use `MEASURE(`BPD Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bpd_compliance_metrics` for governed rate reporting.

snippets.headline: Metric views answer rate questions, while gold adherence tables answer patient-level evidence and care-gap questions.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Each measure has two complementary sources: a compliance metric view for rates and a `gold_adherence_<measure>` table for patient-level detail plus evidence. Use `gsd_compliance_metrics`, `ked_compliance_metrics`, `bpd_compliance_metrics`, `spd_compliance_metrics`, or `eed_compliance_metrics` for governed rates. Use the corresponding `gold_adherence_gsd`, `gold_adherence_ked`, `gold_adherence_bpd`, `gold_adherence_spd`, or `gold_adherence_eed` table when the question asks which patients met a measure, what evidence supports it, or where care gaps exist.

snippets.headline: Age-band reporting for Glycemic Status, Blood Pressure control, and Eye Exam uses three shared adult bands.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The GSD age band logic, which also matches the GSD/BPD/EED metric views, is `CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75' END`. The complete output value list is `18-44`, `45-64`, and `65-75`. Use these exact cut points and labels for GSD, BPD, and EED age-band reporting to match the metric views. The upper band label reflects the 18-75 eligible age range for those measures.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control rates measure results among tested patients, while Glycemic Status compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For GSD, good and poor glycemic control rates are computed only among A1c-tested patients, not all eligible diabetic patients. The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. The poor control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, using the same tested-patient denominator. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

## Definition
The **measurement year (MY)** is the calendar year a HEDIS measure is computed for. Eligibility, the numerator window, and the value-set version are all evaluated relative to it.

* **Current MY:** **2025**, set by the pipeline setting `care.measurement_year`.
* **Age:** evaluated at `period_end` (Dec 31 of the MY).
* **Numerator window:** `period_start`–`period_end` (Jan 1 – Dec 31).
* **Value-set version:** `value_set_segment.measurement_year`.

## Business use
To compare rates across years, also compare the value-set versions in effect; see **Measure Drift**.

## Age is checked on Dec 31 of the measurement year; care must happen between Jan 1 and Dec 31 of that year

Everything is measured against the **measurement year (MY)**, which is the calendar year a measure is computed for. [Measurement Year](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c84e5ba4-05b5-47b2-9126-370c57c488a9?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

- **Age:** checked at `period_end`, which is **December 31 of the MY**. A patient's age on that date decides which age range they fall into.
- **When the care must happen:** between `period_start` and `period_end`, so **January 1 to December 31 of the MY**. "An A1c test in the measurement year" means a test on any date in that span. [Measurement Year](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c4aacb75-c618-44b0-b93e-1d703604ea2f?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **Code lists:** the lists of qualifying lab and drug codes are also versioned by MY, so a measure's definition can change from one year to the next. [Measurement Year](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c4aacb75-c618-44b0-b93e-1d703604ea2f?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### How each measure applies this

| Measure | Age on Dec 31 | Required in Jan 1–Dec 31 |
|---|---|---|
| GSD (blood sugar / A1c testing) | 18–75 | At least one A1c test [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-1dcd1712-1700-4711-82fe-ebc133803e9a) |
| KED (kidney health check) | 18–85 | **Both** an eGFR and a uACR kidney test [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-d3494f59-4cda-47e7-babd-761d66786d55) |
| BPD (blood pressure control) | 18–75 | Most recent blood pressure reading below 140/90 [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-86adf1a5-90f4-4606-ad30-7ecc55cc7aa8) |
| SPD (statin therapy) | 40–75 | A statin dispensed [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-670bc59e-4126-4b88-9bdb-91dd8161a367) |
| EED (eye exam) | 18–75 | A retinal or diabetic eye exam [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5c422ecb-eeb0-4711-a5dc-96599be621c6) |

All five measures start from the same diabetes group: patients with diagnosis codes under E10, E11 or E13. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-6d2030c9-1a4b-4ff7-aa89-ecc48b60f3f9)

### The data uses a different year than the glossary
The glossary says the current measurement year is **2025**. [Measurement Year](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c84e5ba4-05b5-47b2-9126-370c57c488a9?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) But the kidney (KED) measure table currently runs from **2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31** for all 2,802 rows. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2d1cae62539442f897601307310130d9?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_8d101b) So the pipeline appears to have moved to MY2026. If so, ages are now checked on Dec 31, 2026. The glossary may need updating. Also, the 2026 code list for the eGFR kidney test keeps only one test code, while the eGFR results in the data use a different code. That could push 2026 kidney rates down even if testing didn't change. [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

## Definition
The set of patients with a diabetes diagnosis: any ICD-10-CM code that is a **descendant of E10, E11, or E13** (type 1, type 2, and other/specified diabetes).

## How it is resolved
The cohort is resolved semantically, not from a hand-maintained code list. `silver_condition` is joined to `icd10_closure` on `descendant_code` where `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`. One equality join captures the whole subtree (e.g. `E11.21`, `E11.319`); see **Code Subsumption**.

## Data
`silver_diabetes_cohort`: one row per distinct `patient_id`.

## Business use
All five diabetes measures apply their own age band to this cohort. A flat code list would miss specific child codes and undercount every measure.

snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_tables
snippets.content: To filter for notable diagnosis names in `dim_diagnosis`, INCLUDE exactly these five values: `'Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications'`, `'Essential (primary) hypertension'`, `'ST elevation MI involving left main coronary artery'`, `'General adult medical exam without abnormal findings'`, and `'Cerebral infarction, unspecified'`. The exact SQL pattern is `dim_diagnosis.diagnosis_name IN (...)` using the complete list. This is an inclusion filter, not a list of values to exclude. The corresponding CCS category filter is separate and should not be assumed to be interchangeable with diagnosis name filtering.

snippets.headline: Cardiovascular prescribing counts medication event rows attached to encounters with cardiovascular primary diagnoses.
snippets.source: Eval Stress Test - Epic EMR
snippets.content: Medication prescribing for patients with cardiovascular diagnoses is computed by joining event rows to encounters and diagnoses: `fact_clinical_event ce JOIN dim_medication m ON ce.medication_key = m.medication_key JOIN fact_encounter fe ON ce.encounter_key = fe.encounter_key JOIN dim_diagnosis dx ON fe.primary_diagnosis_key = dx.diagnosis_key`. The standard cardiovascular prescription cohort INCLUDES `dx.diagnosis_category = 'Cardiovascular' AND ce.event_type = 'Medication'`. The metric is `COUNT(*) AS prescription_count` grouped by `m.generic_name` and `m.therapeutic_class`. This counts medication clinical-event rows associated with encounters whose primary diagnosis is cardiovascular, not unique patients or active prescriptions.

## Definition
HEDIS measure of statin use in patients with diabetes.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **40–75** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** at least one statin dispensed during the measurement year.
* **Value set:** `SPD_STATIN` (RxNorm **ingredients**, e.g. `36567` simvastatin, `83367` atorvastatin)

## Why subsumption is required
Prescriptions carry RxNorm **clinical-drug** codes (e.g. `312961` *Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet*), not ingredients. A flat ingredient match finds **zero** statins, so SPD resolves ingredients to their clinical drugs through `rxnorm_closure` (see **Code Subsumption**).

## Data
* **Metric view:** `spd_compliance_metrics`

pages_read.body:
**Measure drift** is when a quality measure's *result changes because its definition changed* — not because
the underlying care changed. Value sets are versioned by **measurement year** (`value_set_segment.measurement_year`),
which makes drift explicit, auditable, and reproducible instead of a silent code-list edit.

**Worked example — eGFR code modernization (KED):**
- **MY2025** `KED_EGFR` accepts `98979-8` (CKD-EPI) **and** `33914-3` (MDRD).
- **MY2026** `KED_EGFR` is "modernized" to `98979-8` (CKD-EPI) only.
- The lab data is identical (Synthea records eGFR as `33914-3`, MDRD). Yet eGFR coverage for 2025 observations
  under each value-set version is:

| Value-set version | Patients with eGFR | Codes matched |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | **79** | 33914-3 |
| 2026 | **0** | (none) |

Switching the value set silently erases eGFR coverage — which would collapse the KED rate — with zero change
in actual testing. The demo query is `src/semantic/measure_drift_demo.sql`.

**Why the context layer matters:** because the value set is governed and year-stamped, you can (a) reproduce a
measure exactly as defined in any year, (b) attribute a rate change to a definition change vs. a care change,
and (c) see, before shipping a spec update, which codes you are about to drop.

> HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

## Definition
A lab estimate of how well the kidneys filter blood.

* **Value set:** `KED_EGFR`, containing **`33914-3`** (MDRD-based, the code Synthea emits) and **`98979-8`** (newer CKD-EPI).
* A measure must accept **every** valid code for the concept. Relying on a single code undercounts.

## Data
Conformed into `silver_observation`. Feeds `gold_adherence_ked` as `egfr_flag` and the `eGFR Test Rate` metric.

genie_one_sql:
WITH rx AS (
  SELECT p.patient_id, p.evidence_code, p.evidence_drug, p.evidence_datetime,
         MAX(CASE WHEN rc.ancestor_code <> 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' THEN rc.ancestor_name END) AS ingredient,
         MAX(CASE WHEN rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' THEN rc.ancestor_code END) AS drug_class
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd p
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc
    ON rc.descendant_code = p.evidence_code AND rc.depth > 0
  WHERE p.patient_id = 'fa93c75f-1541-10c2-ea84-f947c8561ce5'
  GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT rx.evidence_drug AS dispensed_drug, rx.evidence_code AS rxcui, rx.ingredient, rx.drug_class,
       pe.predicate, pe.object AS contraindication, pe.source AS protocol_rule,
       vs.segment_name, vs.code AS value_set_code,
       sc.icd10_code AS patient_dx_code, sc.description AS patient_dx, ic.depth,
       COUNT(*) AS dx_records, MIN(sc.onset_date) AS first_onset, MAX(sc.onset_date) AS latest_onset,
       MAX(rx.evidence_datetime) AS statin_order_datetime
FROM rx
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  ON pe.subject = rx.drug_class AND pe.predicate LIKE 'contraindicated%'
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs
  ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic
  ON ic.ancestor_code = vs.code
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc
  ON sc.patient_id = rx.patient_id AND sc.icd10_code = ic.descendant_code
GROUP BY ALL

SELECT 'edge' AS kind, subject AS a, predicate AS b, object AS c, source AS d FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges WHERE subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
UNION ALL
SELECT 'dx', icd10_code, description, CAST(COUNT(*) AS STRING), CONCAT(CAST(MIN(onset_date) AS STRING),' to ',CAST(MAX(onset_date) AS STRING)) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition WHERE patient_id = 'fa93c75f-1541-10c2-ea84-f947c8561ce5' GROUP BY icd10_code, description

snippets.headline: Active population and care gap analyses exclude deceased patients from their denominators.
snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_tables
snippets.content: For active population or care gap analyses, EXCLUDE deceased patients with `dim_patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`. The rule is an exclusion rule: active cohorts should apply `dim_patient.patient_status <> 'Deceased'` or an equivalent NOT filter. The source only identifies one excluded status value, `'Deceased'`; no other patient status values are specified for exclusion. This rule should be applied before calculating active population counts or care gap denominators.

snippets.headline: Open gaps totals the unresolved care gaps across patients in the selected cohort.
snippets.source: main.cedar.mv_patient_risk
snippets.content: The metric `open_gaps` in `main.cedar.mv_patient_risk` is defined exactly as `SUM(source.open_gap_count)`. It represents the total number of open care gaps for the selected patient cohort or grouping. Because this is a summed count over the patient panel, grouping dimensions such as payer, metro, condition, or risk band determine which patients' open gaps contribute to the total.

snippets.headline: At-risk patients are concentrated among recently discharged patients whose seven-day follow-up remains incomplete.
snippets.source: Cedar Population Health
snippets.content: Open care gaps in this asset mean that no 7-day post-discharge follow-up has been completed. The at-risk cluster should be investigated as recently discharged patients with open gaps, using `main.cedar.gold_patient_panel` grouped by `primary_condition` and `risk_band`, and `main.cedar.gold_open_atrisk` grouped by `has_open_followup` and `risk_band`. For questions like "what do these at-risk patients have in common," the intended pattern is to show confinement to recently discharged patients with open follow-up gaps rather than treating the whole 30K-patient panel as uniformly at risk. The sample aggregation pattern is `SELECT has_open_followup, risk_band, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM main.cedar.gold_open_atrisk GROUP BY has_open_followup, risk_band ORDER BY patient_count DESC`.

snippets.headline: The deceased status rate identifies inactive patients who would inflate active-population allergy and care-gap reporting.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics
snippets.content: `Active Patient Deceased Status Exclusion Rate` is defined as `SUM(CASE WHEN patient.patient_status = 'Deceased' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id), 0)`. The numerator counts allergy-population rows where the joined patient dimension has `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`, while the denominator is distinct patients with allergy records (`COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id)`). The measure is intended as a quality/control indicator to ensure active-population metrics and care gap reports are not inflated by patients flagged as deceased; if computing active-population allergy metrics directly, analysts should EXCLUDE `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`.

snippets.headline: Metabolic abnormality comparisons by insurance require more than twenty patients with any lab result.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: For metabolic abnormality comparisons by primary insurance in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics`, the curated query suppresses small denominators. Include only insurance groups where `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Any Lab Result`) > 20`. The numerator-like companion measure is `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Abnormal Metabolic Results`)`, and the rate is `MEASURE(`High and Critically High Metabolic Lab Result Patient Rate`)`. The exact threshold is `> 20`, and it is applied with `HAVING` after grouping by `Primary Insurance`.

snippets.headline: Open gaps totals unresolved care gaps across recently discharged patients, not the number of patients with gaps.
snippets.source: Cedar Population Health.lvdash.json
snippets.content: Open gaps for the recent-discharge exposure cohort is `SUM(open_gap_count)` from `gold_patient_panel` after `WHERE days_since_discharge <= 30`. The metric sums the number of unresolved care gaps across included patient-panel rows; it is not a count of patients with at least one gap. Use the same `days_since_discharge <= 30` scope when comparing open gaps with exposure or risk-band counts.

snippets.headline: Patient population counts come from the patient-level view because it avoids fact-table fan-out inflation.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` is sourced directly from the patient dimension and is the correct source for unduplicated patient population counts. Because it does not join to encounter or clinical event fact tables, counts such as `MEASURE(`Total Patients`)`, `MEASURE(`Active Patients`)`, and `MEASURE(`Deceased Patients`)` reflect true patient population rather than activity-driven duplicates. Use it for demographic distribution and chronic disease burden by age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, geography, and patient status. Do not use encounter or clinical event views for pure population denominators unless the question explicitly asks for patients with activity.

snippets.headline: Headline readmission exposure, open care gaps, and critical patient counts come from the dashboard-aligned risk view.
snippets.source: Cedar Population Health
snippets.content: Use `main.cedar.mv_patient_risk` as the canonical source for headline dashboard numbers because it uses the same definitions as the dashboard tiles. Specifically, answer "What's our readmission exposure?" with `MEASURE(readmission_exposure)`, "How many open care gaps?" with `MEASURE(open_gaps)`, and "How many patients are critical?" with `MEASURE(critical_count)`. Do not recompute these headline numbers directly from lower-level tables when the question asks for the dashboard-aligned totals. Example pattern: `SELECT MEASURE(readmission_exposure) AS readmission_exposure, MEASURE(open_gaps) AS open_gaps FROM main.cedar.mv_patient_risk`.

snippets.headline: Active-population allergy analyses should exclude deceased patients to avoid inflating care-gap metrics.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics
snippets.content: `Patient Status` maps to `patient.patient_status` and identifies active versus inactive patient populations, with examples including `Active` and `Deceased`. The view's deceased-status measure treats patients with `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'` as records that can inflate active-population metrics and care gap reporting. For active-population analyses, EXCLUDE `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`; the source does not provide a complete list of all possible patient status values.

snippets.headline: The active-to-deceased ratio compares active and deceased patient counts within each insurance and status group.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: The active-to-deceased patient ratio in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` is computed as `MEASURE(`Active Patients`) / NULLIF(MEASURE(`Deceased Patients`), 0)`. The curated query groups by `Primary Insurance` and `Patient Status`, then orders by this ratio descending. The denominator is deceased patients in the same insurance-and-status group, not all patients and not total patients. `NULLIF(..., 0)` makes the ratio null for groups with zero deceased patients rather than dividing by zero.

snippets.headline: Patient demographics support population, encounter, and event questions, but each denominator requires its matching view.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: Patient demographic dimensions appear in all three metric views, but the correct source depends on the analytical denominator. `Patient Sex`, `Patient Race`, `Primary Insurance`, and `Patient Status` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` should be used for pure population counts such as total active or deceased patients. The same demographic fields in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.encounter_metrics` and `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` should be used only when the population is explicitly scoped to encounters or lab/clinical events. This prevents mixing a patient denominator with an encounter or event numerator.

snippets.headline: Patient PT-0000214 is the canonical high-risk heart-failure example with a recent discharge and open follow-up gap.
snippets.source: Cedar Population Health
snippets.content: Patient `PT-0000214` is the canonical high-risk example patient for this Genie and should be inspected in `main.cedar.gold_open_atrisk` and `main.cedar.gold_intervention_recommendations`. The curated example states this patient is HF, was discharged about 8 days ago, has an open follow-up gap, and has high readmission risk. Accepted lookup patterns are `SELECT * FROM main.cedar.gold_open_atrisk WHERE patient_id = 'PT-0000214'` and `SELECT patient_id, recommended_intervention, predicted_risk_reduction, predicted_net_value_usd FROM main.cedar.gold_intervention_recommendations WHERE patient_id = 'PT-0000214'`. Treat this as a specific demonstration/hero patient, not a general filter for all risk analysis.

snippets.headline: Metabolic lab analyses include only glucose and hemoglobin A1C results.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: Metabolic lab flags in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` cover only two event descriptions. The inclusion list is exactly `Event Description IN ('Glucose', 'Hemoglobin A1C')`; no other lab event descriptions are part of the metabolic lab flag definition in this Genie space. The curated metabolic measures include `MEASURE(`High and Critically High Metabolic Lab Result Patient Rate`)`, `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Abnormal Metabolic Results`)`, and `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Any Lab Result`)`. Use this filter concept when analyzing metabolic abnormality rates by patient race or primary insurance.

snippets.headline: Encounters per Patient shows encounter intensity by dividing encounter volume by unique patients in the same segment.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: `Encounters per Patient` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` is an average utilization intensity measure at the selected dimension grain. Its queryable expression is ``MEASURE(`Encounters per Patient`)``; the definition-time expression over the source is `COUNT(1) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.patient_key), 0)`. The numerator is total encounters and the denominator is distinct patients within the same selected grouping, not calendar days or all patients in the system. Use this named measure rather than dividing `MEASURE(`Encounter Count`)` by `MEASURE(`Patient Count`)` unless you intentionally need equivalent arithmetic outside the measure calls at the same grain.

snippets.headline: Patients using both hospital and virtual care must have at least one inpatient encounter and one telehealth encounter.
snippets.source: (Clone) (Clone) Blank test space tables
snippets.content: The cohort of patients who used both hospital inpatient care and virtual care is defined after aggregating encounters by patient. Join `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.fact_encounter e` to `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.dim_patient p` on `e.patient_key = p.patient_key`, then compute `SUM(CASE WHEN e.encounter_type = 'Inpatient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inpatient_count` and `SUM(CASE WHEN e.encounter_type = 'Telehealth' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS telehealth_count`. INCLUDE only patients with `HAVING inpatient_count > 0 AND telehealth_count > 0`; both thresholds use the exact operator `> 0`. This is a patient-level cohort, not an encounter-level filter, so filtering rows with `encounter_type IN ('Inpatient', 'Telehealth')` alone does not prove a patient had both types.

pages_read.body:
## Definition
A **care gap** is an eligible patient who has not received the care a measure requires.

* **Denominator (eligible):** the patients a measure applies to.
* **Numerator (compliant):** the eligible patients who received the required care.
* **Status:** **MET** if the patient is in the numerator; otherwise **NOT_MET**, which means an open care gap.

## Data
Each `gold_adherence_<measure>` row holds one patient's status plus **record-level evidence** (test date, code, and value), so every MET or NOT_MET is traceable.

## Business use
Gap lists drive outreach. Closing a gap moves the patient into the numerator, which raises the measure's **Compliance Rate**.

- **EED, eye exam:** no retinal or diabetic eye exam on record in 2026. To close it, schedule the exam.

- **SPD, statin therapy:** Simvastatin 10 MG was dispensed on 2026-08-15.
