## 198 patients are on a statin despite a contraindicating diagnosis

**198 patients** have a statin order and also have at least one diagnosis of their own that the care protocol lists as a statin contraindication. That's about 4% of the 4,741 patients with a statin order. Every one of them is flagged for **pregnancy**, under rule CP sec4 ("statin class `contraindicatedWith` CONTRA_PREGNANCY"). [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_421c51) [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_bf7445)

<!-- begin-embedded:query_170085 -->
| contraindication | protocol_rule | icd10_code | diagnosis | patients | statins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | Z34.90 | Normal pregnancy (finding) | 198 | atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O00.1 | Tubal pregnancy (disorder) | 10 | atorvastatin, simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O15.9 | Eclampsia in pregnancy (disorder) | 10 | simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O26.9 | Complication occurring during pregnancy (disorder) | 2 | atorvastatin, simvastatin |
<!-- end-embedded:query_170085 -->

- **The flag comes from "Normal pregnancy" in every case.** All 198 patients have Z34.90 on their record. A few also have tubal pregnancy (10), eclampsia (10) or a pregnancy complication (2). Because some patients have more than one of these codes, the rows above add up to more than 198.
- **No one is flagged for liver disease.** The protocol's other statin contraindication covers liver disease codes K70 and K74, but no patient has either code recorded. [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_519543) [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_ab29f0)
- **Checked against two other sources.** The raw medication orders also give 198 patients. Only **20** of the 198 are statin users in the SPD measure (statin therapy for patients with diabetes), which covers just diabetes patients aged 40–75. [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_519543)

### How the match works
Each statin order is traced up to the statin drug class. The class is linked to the protocol's contraindication rules, each rule to its list of diagnosis codes, and each code family to the specific codes on the patient's record. This is the same path used in the earlier trace for a single patient (simvastatin with Z34.90). [Single-patient statin contraindication trace](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/ceced28428414c8e900d9fe9bb1753a9?o=3464092709171785)

### What this count doesn't check
The protocol rule matches on the diagnosis code alone. It doesn't check whether the pregnancy overlaps the statin order in time. In the earlier single-patient trace, the pregnancy was recorded years before the statin order. [Single-patient statin contraindication trace](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/ceced28428414c8e900d9fe9bb1753a9?o=3464092709171785) So 198 is everyone the rule flags. The number with a pregnancy at the same time as the statin is likely lower; a clinician should review these patients before treating them as active conflicts.
genie_one_sql: SELECT table_schema, table_name, substr(comment,1,200) AS c FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema IN ('care_protocol_terminology','care_protocol') AND table_name NOT LIKE '\\_\\_%' ORDER BY 1,2
SELECT * FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges
SELECT * FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment WHERE segment_id LIKE 'CONTRA%' OR segment_id LIKE '%STATIN%'

WITH statin_rx AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc
    ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'),
contra AS (
  SELECT pe.object AS segment_id, pe.source, vs.code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs
    ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
  WHERE pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'),
via_closure AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.patient_id, c.segment_id
  FROM statin_rx s
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc ON sc.patient_id = s.patient_id
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic ON ic.descendant_code = sc.icd10_code
  JOIN contra c ON c.code = ic.ancestor_code),
via_prefix AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.patient_id, c.segment_id
  FROM statin_rx s
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc ON sc.patient_id = s.patient_id
  JOIN contra c ON sc.icd10_code LIKE concat(c.code, '%'))
SELECT 'closure' AS method, segment_id, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS patients FROM via_closure GROUP BY ALL
UNION ALL SELECT 'closure', 'ANY', COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM via_closure
UNION ALL SELECT 'prefix', segment_id, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM via_prefix GROUP BY ALL
UNION ALL SELECT 'prefix', 'ANY', COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM via_prefix
UNION ALL SELECT 'statin_patients', 'ALL', COUNT(*) FROM statin_rx

WITH contra AS (
  SELECT pe.object AS segment_id, vs.code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs
    ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
  WHERE pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'),
contra_pat AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.patient_id, c.segment_id
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic ON ic.descendant_code = sc.icd10_code
  JOIN contra c ON c.code = ic.ancestor_code),
bronze AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'),
spd AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.patient_id FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd p
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc ON rc.descendant_code = p.evidence_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN')
SELECT 'bronze_order_med' AS statin_source, COUNT(DISTINCT b.patient_id) AS flagged FROM bronze b JOIN contra_pat c USING (patient_id)
UNION ALL SELECT 'gold_adherence_spd', COUNT(DISTINCT s.patient_id) FROM spd s JOIN contra_pat c USING (patient_id)
UNION ALL SELECT concat('any patient with ', segment_id), COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM contra_pat GROUP BY segment_id
UNION ALL SELECT 'hepatic K70/K74 codes in silver_condition', COUNT(*) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition WHERE icd10_code LIKE 'K70%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'K74%'

WITH rx AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id, rc2.ancestor_name AS statin_ingredient
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc2 ON rc2.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc2.depth > 0 AND rc2.ancestor_code <> 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'),
contra AS (
  SELECT pe.object AS segment_id, pe.source, vs.code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
  WHERE pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith')
SELECT c.segment_id AS contraindication, c.source AS protocol_rule, sc.icd10_code, sc.description AS diagnosis,
       COUNT(DISTINCT rx.patient_id) AS patients,
       concat_ws(', ', array_sort(collect_set(rx.statin_ingredient))) AS statins
FROM rx
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc ON sc.patient_id = rx.patient_id
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic ON ic.descendant_code = sc.icd10_code
JOIN contra c ON c.code = ic.ancestor_code
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY patients DESC

snippets.headline: Metabolic lab analyses include only glucose and hemoglobin A1C results.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: Metabolic lab flags in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` cover only two event descriptions. The inclusion list is exactly `Event Description IN ('Glucose', 'Hemoglobin A1C')`; no other lab event descriptions are part of the metabolic lab flag definition in this Genie space. snippets.headline: Patient population counts come from the patient-level view because it avoids fact-table fan-out inflation.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` is sourced directly from the patient dimension and is the correct source for unduplicated patient population counts. Because it does not join to encounter or clinical event fact tables, counts such as `MEASURE(`Total Patients`)`, `MEASURE(`Active Patients`)`, and `MEASURE(`Deceased Patients`)` reflect true patient population rather than activity-driven duplicates. Use it for demographic distribution and chronic disease burden by age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, geography, and patient status. Do not use encounter or clinical event views for pure population denominators unless the question explicitly asks for patients with activity.

snippets.headline: Abnormal lab burden by race and ethnicity counts distinct affected patients rather than raw lab events.
snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_mvs
snippets.content: Abnormal lab burden by patient race and ethnicity in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` is measured with distinct-patient counts, not raw clinical-event counts. The verified demographic pattern groups by `Patient Race` and `Patient Ethnicity`, then compares `MEASURE(`Distinct Patients with Critical Abnormal Labs`)`, `MEASURE(`Distinct Patients with Abnormal Results`)`, and `MEASURE(`Total Distinct Patients`)`. It includes only demographic groups with abnormal-result patients using `HAVING MEASURE(`Distinct Patients with Abnormal Results`) > 0`. Use this pattern for demographic disparity questions about abnormal or critical abnormal lab patients; do not substitute event counts as the denominator or numerator.

snippets.headline: Serious adverse events count CTCAE grade three or higher events and are normalized by enrolled patients.
snippets.source: test clinical trial space
snippets.content: Serious Adverse Events are defined as adverse events with CTCAE grade `>= 3`. In `eswanson_demo.clinical_trials.trial_portfolio_metrics`, use `MEASURE(`Serious Adverse Event Count`)` for the serious adverse event numerator. For sponsor-level serious adverse event burden per enrolled patient, compute `MEASURE(`Serious Adverse Event Count`) / NULLIF(MEASURE(`Enrolled Patient Count`), 0)` and apply `HAVING MEASURE(`Enrolled Patient Count`) > 0` to avoid zero-denominator groups. The denominator is enrolled patients aggregated at the same grouping grain, such as sponsor or biomarker-stratification status, not the number of trials.

snippets.headline: Encounters per Patient shows encounter intensity by dividing encounter volume by unique patients in the same segment.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: `Encounters per Patient` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` is an average utilization intensity measure at the selected dimension grain. Its queryable expression is ``MEASURE(`Encounters per Patient`)``; the definition-time expression over the source is `COUNT(1) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.patient_key), 0)`. The numerator is total encounters and the denominator is distinct patients within the same selected grouping, not calendar days or all patients in the system. Use this named measure rather than dividing `MEASURE(`Encounter Count`)` by `MEASURE(`Patient Count`)` unless you intentionally need equivalent arithmetic outside the measure calls at the same grain.

snippets.headline: The active-to-deceased ratio compares active and deceased patient counts within each insurance and status group.

pages_read.body:
**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure for assessing kidney
health in diabetic patients. Its numerator is **compound** — it requires two different tests in the same year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–85** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** **both** of the following in the measurement year:
  1. an **eGFR** (estimated glomerular filtration rate) test — value set `KED_EGFR`, and
  2. a **uACR** (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) test — value set `KED_UACR`.

A patient is **MET** only when **both** components are present; missing either is a care gap. Because the two
components are tracked separately, the **eGFR Test Rate** and **uACR Test Rate** are each exposed in
`ked_compliance_metrics` alongside the combined **KED Compliance Rate**. In this demo uACR is the limiting
component (eGFR ~92%, uACR ~51%, combined ~51%).

> The eGFR value set spans LOINC vintages (e.g. `33914-3` MDRD and `98979-8`) — a reminder that value sets
> evolve and a measure must accept all valid codes for the concept. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

## Definition
HEDIS measure of kidney-health evaluation in patients with diabetes. Its numerator is **compound**: it requires two different lab tests in the same year.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **18–85** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** **both** an **eGFR** test and a **uACR** test in the measurement year. Missing either one is a care gap.
* **Value sets:** `KED_EGFR`, `KED_UACR`

## Data
* **Metrics** in `ked_compliance_metrics`: `KED Compliance Rate` (combined), `eGFR Test Rate`, `uACR Test Rate`
* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_ked` (`egfr_flag`, `uacr_flag`)

## Examples
Demo rates: eGFR \~92%, uACR \~51%, combined \~51%. The combined rate tracks uACR.

---

pages_read.body:
## Definition
The set of patients with a diabetes diagnosis: any ICD-10-CM code that is a **descendant of E10, E11, or E13** (type 1, type 2, and other/specified diabetes).

## How it is resolved
The cohort is resolved semantically, not from a hand-maintained code list. `silver_condition` is joined to `icd10_closure` on `descendant_code` where `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`. One equality join captures the whole subtree (e.g. `E11.21`, `E11.319`); see **Code Subsumption**.

## Data
`silver_diabetes_cohort`: one row per distinct `patient_id`.

## Business use
All five diabetes measures apply their own age band to this cohort. A flat code list would miss specific child codes and undercount every measure.

## KED: who's eligible and what counts as compliant

**Eligible (denominator):** patients in the **Diabetes Cohort** who are **18–85 years old as of the end of the measurement year** (December 31). [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) [KED — Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/9edbb1f7-62bd-405e-9bb6-fa9413b7d243?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- A patient is in the Diabetes Cohort if they have any ICD-10-CM diagnosis code under **E10, E11, or E13**, including every child code (for example, E11.21). [Diabetes Cohort](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/402e8af3-3e5a-4a46-aa36-22dcd8df5e64?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

**Compliant (numerator):** the patient needs **both** of these tests in the same measurement year:
1. an **eGFR** test (value set `KED_EGFR`), and
2. a **uACR** test (urine albumin-creatinine ratio, value set `KED_UACR`).

A patient counts as met only if both tests are present. Missing either one is a care gap. [KED — Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/9edbb1f7-62bd-405e-9bb6-fa9413b7d243?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

**Notes:**
- **Accept every eGFR code version.** eGFR tests are recorded under more than one LOINC code (33914-3 MDRD and 98979-8), and all of them count. Common uACR codes include 14959-1. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_ked?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- **uACR is the test that holds the rate down.** About 92% of patients have an eGFR test but only about 51% have a uACR test, so the combined KED rate (about 51%) closely follows uACR. [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- **Where to find the data:**
  - Patient-level detail is in [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_ked?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785), which has one row per eligible patient. Use `eligible_flag` for eligibility and `egfr_flag` / `uacr_flag` for each test.
  - The rates (combined KED Compliance Rate, eGFR Test Rate, uACR Test Rate) are in [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_semantic/ked_compliance_metrics?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785).
- This setup follows HEDIS but is a demo and is not NCQA-certified.

This rate answers the share of active allergy records classified as severe and should not be interpreted as the share of patients with any severe allergy unless redefined with distinct `source.pat_id`.

snippets.headline: Severe drug allergy counts are patient-level and stricter than the broader severe-or-moderate allergy filter.

snippets.content: Patients with Severe Drug Allergies is defined by the condition `allergy.allergen_type = 'Drug' AND allergy.severity = 'Severe'` and is intended to count distinct patients. The snippet code is `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN allergy.allergen_type = 'Drug' AND allergy.severity = 'Severe' THEN 'allergy.pat_id' END)`, but the quoted `'allergy.pat_id'` is a literal string and would count at most one value; the intended patient-level denominator should use the column `allergy.pat_id` without quotes. ## Definition
HEDIS measure of whether patients with diabetes had their glycemic status (**HbA1c**) assessed during the measurement year.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **18–75** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** at least one HbA1c test in the measurement year.
* **Value set:** `GSD_A1C_TEST`
* **Control bands (latest A1c):** good control **< 8%**, poor control **> 9%**.

* **Metric:** `GSD Compliance Rate` in `gsd_compliance_metrics`
* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_gsd` (MET / NOT_MET with test evidence)

onto_poor_control_denominator.genie_one_answer:
## GSD Poor Control Rate: denominator is tested patients only, and the threshold is A1c > 9.0%

The GSD poor-control rate does **not** use all eligible patients. Its denominator is only the eligible patients who had **at least one A1c test in the measurement year**. A patient counts as poorly controlled when their **latest A1c in the measurement year is above 9.0%**. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_semantic/gsd_compliance_metrics?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/04bb09814a1e45969c215ccca824eec9?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_5bdf92)

### How it's calculated
This comes from the certified GSD compliance metric view:

| Piece | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Poor Control Rate** | Poor Control Patients ÷ Compliant Patients |
| **Poor Control Patients** (top of the fraction) | Patients whose latest A1c is **> 9.0%**. A result of exactly 9.0% doesn't count. |
| **Compliant Patients** (bottom of the fraction) | Eligible patients with an A1c test in the measurement year |
| **Eligible Patients** (not used in this rate) | Diabetes patients aged 18–75 at the end of the measurement year |

[Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/04bb09814a1e45969c215ccca824eec9?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_5bdf92)

### What this means in practice
- **Untested patients are left out of the rate.** A patient with no A1c result can't be scored for control. They show up as a gap in the separate **GSD Compliance Rate** (tested ÷ eligible), not in the poor-control rate.
- If you want poor control as a share of **all** eligible patients, divide Poor Control Patients by Eligible Patients. That number will be lower whenever some eligible patients weren't tested.
- The **good control** group is A1c **< 8.0%**. Patients from 8.0% to 9.0% fall in neither group. [GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/1045ab28-3390-4c2f-a056-381c1019c345?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

There's also a separate glossary entry, "Poorly controlled diabetes." It uses the same >9% threshold but is framed as a share of all health-center diabetes patients, so its denominator may differ from the GSD rate. [Poorly controlled diabetes](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/89de86e4-4d18-4848-9c16-cfa8b107ba8b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) The GSD view is labeled HEDIS-aligned, not NCQA-certified.

snippets.headline: Standard patient age bands split patients into under 18, three adult ranges, seniors, and unknown age.
snippets.source: test space tables
snippets.content: Patient Age Band has a curated reusable expression: `CASE WHEN dim_patient.age_at_last_visit < 18 THEN '<18' WHEN dim_patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 18 AND 34 THEN '18-34' WHEN dim_patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 35 AND 49 THEN '35-49' WHEN dim_patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 50 AND 64 THEN '50-64' WHEN dim_patient.age_at_last_visit >= 65 THEN '65+' ELSE 'Unknown' END`. This age band is a population segmentation dimension with buckets `<18`, `18-34`, `35-49`, `50-64`, `65+`, and `Unknown`. The bucket boundaries are inclusive where `BETWEEN` is used, so ages 18 and 34 both fall in `18-34`, and age 65 falls in `65+`. Use this standard expression when a question asks for patient age band, age group, age bucket, age category, or age segment without specifying alternative labels.

snippets.headline: Age at last visit has slightly different labels across views but represents the same patient age concept.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: `Patient Age at Last Visit` and `Age at Last Visit` refer to the same age concept across the Genie space, despite the naming difference. The encounter and clinical event views use `Patient Age at Last Visit`, while the patient chronic disease view exposes `Age at Last Visit` and `MEASURE(`Average Age at Last Visit`)`. When comparing age distributions across views, treat these as the same business concept but keep the view-specific grain in mind. For pure average patient age by insurance, use `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` with `MEASURE(`Average Age at Last Visit`)`.

snippets.headline: Two patient age groupings exist, and their adult boundaries differ for standard segmentation versus charge analysis.
snippets.source: test space tables
snippets.content: There are two different age-grouping definitions in the space, and they answer different questions. The standard Patient Age Band uses `<18`, `18-34`, `35-49`, `50-64`, `65+`, and `Unknown` from `dim_patient.age_at_last_visit`; a separate charges-by-age example uses `Pediatric (<18)`, `Young Adult (18-39)`, `Middle-Aged (40-64)`, `Senior (65+)`, and `Unknown`. Use the standard Patient Age Band for generic segmentation requests, but use the charges-by-age grouping only when reproducing that specific encounter-count and average-total-charges analysis. Do not mix the boundaries: ages 35-39 and 50-64 are assigned differently across the two definitions.

snippets.headline: Patient age comparisons remove the DICOM year suffix and cast the result to an integer.
snippets.source: Pixels - Genie
snippets.content: Patient age in DICOM metadata is stored as a string that may include a year suffix such as `'Y'`, so numeric age filters must normalize it first. The accepted expression is `TRY_CAST(REPLACE(variant_get(meta, "$\." || main.pixels_solacc.retrieve_dicom_tag('patient age').TAG || '.Value[0]', 'STRING'), 'Y', '') AS INTEGER) AS patient_age`. Use this derived integer for age comparisons, for example the verified mammogram query applies `TRY_CAST(REPLACE(variant_get(meta, "$\." || main.pixels_solacc.retrieve_dicom_tag('patient age').TAG || '.Value[0]' , 'STRING'), "Y", "") AS INTEGER) > 50`. Do not compare the raw DICOM age string directly to numeric thresholds.

snippets.headline: Senior encounter reporting identifies patients aged 65 or older at their last recorded visit.
snippets.source: (Clone) (Clone) Blank test space tables
snippets.content: The recurring senior-patient encounter cohort in this asset uses `dim_patient.age_at_last_visit >= 65` after joining encounters to patients with `fact_encounter.patient_key = dim_patient.patient_key`. This is a filter on age at the patient's last visit, not age at each individual encounter date. The sample summary groups the senior cohort by `fact_encounter.encounter_type` and reports `COUNT(*) AS encounters`, `ROUND(AVG(e.total_charges), 0) AS avg_charges`, and `ROUND(AVG(e.los_days), 1) AS avg_los`. Do not infer encounter-time age from `birth_date` for this curated cohort unless the user explicitly asks for age at encounter.

snippets.headline: Year-to-date encounter analysis starts at the current calendar year’s first encounter date key.
snippets.source: test space tables
snippets.content: Year-to-date encounter analysis is filtered by INCLUDING rows where `fact_encounter.encounter_date_key >= CAST(DATE_FORMAT(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', CURRENT_DATE), 'yyyyMMdd') AS INT)`. This filter compares the encounter's integer date key to the first day of the current calendar year in `YYYYMMDD` integer form. The date basis is encounter date, not discharge date or event timestamp. Use this when the question asks for encounters year-to-date.

snippets.headline: Active patient demographics use five fixed age brackets and include only patients with active status.
snippets.source: Eval Stress Test - Epic EMR
snippets.content: Active-patient demographic cohorts are defined with `dp.patient_status = 'Active'` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.dim_patient`. The standard age brackets shown are EXACTLY: `age_at_last_visit < 18` as `'Under 18'`, `age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 18 AND 34` as `'18-34'`, `age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 35 AND 54` as `'35-54'`, `age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 55 AND 74` as `'55-74'`, and all remaining patients as `'75 and older'`. The final bucket therefore includes `age_at_last_visit >= 75` and any records not captured by the earlier numeric predicates. These brackets are grouped with `dp.sex` for active patient counts.

snippets.headline: Patient Age Group segments patients by age at last visit into six fixed reporting bands.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics
snippets.content: The `Patient Age Group` dimension is derived as `CASE WHEN patient.age_at_last_visit < 18 THEN 'Under 18' WHEN patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 18 AND 34 THEN '18-34' WHEN patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 35 AND 49 THEN '35-49' WHEN patient.age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 50 AND 64 THEN '50-64' WHEN patient.age_at_last_visit >= 65 THEN '65+' ELSE 'Unknown' END`. The complete age-band labels are exactly `'Under 18'`, `'18-34'`, `'35-49'`, `'50-64'`, `'65+'`, and `'Unknown'`. The bands are based on age at last visit from the patient dimension, not age at allergy onset, noted date, or current date.

snippets.headline: Patient demographics include protected health information and age reflects the most recent visit rather than current age.
snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_tables
snippets.content: `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.dim_patient` contains patient demographic, geographic, insurance, and identifier attributes and is used broadly across encounter, chronic disease, clinical event, inpatient, and financial reporting. It contains protected health information (PII/PHI), including identifiers such as `pat_id`, `pat_mrn_id`, and `birth_date`. Analysts should apply appropriate access governance and avoid unnecessary exposure of patient-identifying fields. `age_at_last_visit` represents the patient's age at their most recent visit, not their current age at query time.

snippets.headline: Patient age groups use fixed clinical reporting bands based on age at the patient’s last visit.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: The `Age Group` dimension in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` is a curated age-band mapping based on `pat.age_at_last_visit`, not a raw age field. The complete definition-time mapping is: `< 18` maps to `'Pediatric (0-17)'`; `BETWEEN 18 AND 39` maps to `'Young Adult (18-39)'`; `BETWEEN 40 AND 64` maps to `'Middle Age (40-64)'`; `>= 65` maps to `'Senior (65+)'`; all other cases map to `'Unknown'`. Query the metric view using the exposed dimension name `` `Age Group` ``; do not reference `pat.age_at_last_visit` against the metric view. This dimension is intended for demographic segmentation of patient utilization and equity analyses.

snippets.headline: Age and insurance analyses use four fixed age bands based on age at last visit.
snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_tables
snippets.content: Age-band encounter analysis uses `dim_patient.age_at_last_visit` with four exact buckets: `age_at_last_visit < 30` maps to `'Under 30'`, `age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 30 AND 49` maps to `'30-49'`, `age_at_last_visit BETWEEN 50 AND 64` maps to `'50-64'`, and all remaining values map to `'65 and Over'`. The verified query groups those age bands with `dim_patient.primary_insurance`. It reports `COUNT(fe.encounter_key) AS total_encounters` and `ROUND(AVG(fe.patient_paid), 2) AS avg_patient_paid`. The denominator for average patient paid is encounter rows within each age-band and insurance group, not distinct patients.

snippets.headline: Year-over-year amendment trends use the extracted amendment year instead of parsing raw amendment dates.
snippets.source: test clinical trial space
snippets.content: For year-over-year protocol amendment trend analysis in `eswanson_demo.clinical_trials.protocol_amendment_metrics`, use the pre-extracted `Amendment Year` field rather than parsing `Amendment Date`. The curated guidance says amendment dates span approximately a decade and period comparisons should filter by `Amendment Year`. A standard trend query groups by `Amendment Year` and `Trial Phase` and reports `MEASURE(`Eligibility Criteria Amendment Count`)` with `MEASURE(`Total Amendments`)`. Use `Amendment Date` only when an analysis specifically needs date-level detail rather than year comparisons.

snippets.headline: Patient population counts come from the patient-level view because it avoids fact-table fan-out inflation.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_chronic_disease_metrics` is sourced directly from the patient dimension and is the correct source for unduplicated patient population counts. Because it does not join to encounter or clinical event fact tables, counts such as `MEASURE(`Total Patients`)`, `MEASURE(`Active Patients`)`, and `MEASURE(`Deceased Patients`)` reflect true patient population rather than activity-driven duplicates. Use it for demographic distribution and chronic disease burden by age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, geography, and patient status. Do not use encounter or clinical event views for pure population denominators unless the question explicitly asks for patients with activity.

snippets.headline: Amendment and enrollment timelines are calendar-based, unlike adverse event timing fields measured in study days.
snippets.source: test mv space
snippets.content: Amendment dates and enrollment dates are calendar dates, unlike adverse-event study-day fields. Use calendar-period grouping on amendment and enrollment fields, including fields such as `Amendment Date`, `Amendment Year Month`, and `Enrollment Date`, when reporting by month, quarter, or year. This distinction matters because protocol-relative AE days cannot be mixed directly with amendment or enrollment calendar dates on a shared time axis.

pages_read.body:
## Definition
The **measurement year (MY)** is the calendar year a HEDIS measure is computed for. Eligibility, the numerator window, and the value-set version are all evaluated relative to it.

* **Current MY:** **2025**, set by the pipeline setting `care.measurement_year`.
* **Age:** evaluated at `period_end` (Dec 31 of the MY).
* **Numerator window:** `period_start`–`period_end` (Jan 1 – Dec 31).
* **Value-set version:** `value_set_segment.measurement_year`.

## Business use
To compare rates across years, also compare the value-set versions in effect; see **Measure Drift**.

- In this demo the MY is **2025** (configured via the pipeline setting `care.measurement_year`).
- Age is evaluated at **period_end** (Dec 31 of the MY); the numerator window is `period_start`–`period_end`

- Value sets carry a `measurement_year`, so a measure's definition can change year over year — the basis of

pages_read.name: Measurement Year

pages_read.body:
## Definition
**HEDIS** is a standardized set of healthcare quality measures. Each measure defines an eligible population (denominator) and the care those patients should receive (numerator), evaluated over a measurement year.

## Measures in this domain
| Measure | What it checks | Eligible ages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSD | HbA1c test in the year | 18–75 |
| KED | Both eGFR and uACR tests in the year | 18–85 |
| EED | Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year | 18–75 |
| BPD | Latest BP reading < 140/90 mmHg | 18–75 |
| SPD | At least one statin dispensed | 40–75 |

All five measures use the **Diabetes Cohort** as their base population.

## How the pieces fit
* **Measure → Care Gap:** patient-level MET / NOT_MET status.
* **Measure → Compliance Rate:** aggregate compliant ÷ eligible.
* **Measure → Value Set:** the codes that define each numerator, versioned by **Measurement Year**.

---
_HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified. Value sets are hand-curated, not NCQA/VSAC._

onto_age_and_window.genie_one_answer:
## Age is checked on Dec 31 of the measurement year, and care must happen within that same calendar year

Eligibility age is measured **once, on the last day of the measurement year** (`period_end`, which is December 31). The required care has to happen **inside that year, from January 1 (`period_start`) to December 31 (`period_end`)**. [Measurement Year](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c84e5ba4-05b5-47b2-9126-370c57c488a9?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) [Measurement Year](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c4aacb75-c618-44b0-b93e-1d703604ea2f?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

The measurement year also decides which version of each value set (the code lists that define each measure) is used. So when you compare rates across years, check whether those code lists changed between them. [Measurement Year](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c84e5ba4-05b5-47b2-9126-370c57c488a9?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

## Age range and required care by measure (age as of Dec 31)

| Measure | Eligible ages | Required care during the year |
|---|---|---|
| GSD | 18–75 | At least one A1c test |
| KED | 18–85 | **Both** an eGFR test and a uACR test |
| EED | 18–75 | A retinal or diabetic eye exam |
| BPD | 18–75 | The **most recent** blood pressure reading of the year is under 140/90 (both numbers from the same reading) |
| SPD | 40–75 | At least one statin dispensed |
| SSD | 18–64 | A glucose or HbA1c screen. This is a separate group of patients with serious mental illness who take antipsychotics, not the diabetes group |

[HEDIS](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/dc04d5d6-2d8b-470e-95a4-4e81e297d7ad?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) [Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dmvm)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1d63eaf1e148aaca3e207c7499c1a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

## Two things to keep in mind

- **The data is on 2026, but the glossary says 2025.** The glossary describes the current measurement year as 2025. The current data, however, is all for measurement year 2026, running 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. Patient ages in the data stay exactly within each measure's range (for example, 40–75 for SPD and 18–85 for KED). The glossary page looks out of date. [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/07d1138356e2482cb4d39984a0474f29?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_ade227)
- **EED is stricter here than full HEDIS.** Full HEDIS also counts a negative eye screen from the year before. This setup only counts exams within the measurement year. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_eed?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

These definitions follow HEDIS but are a demo setup, not certified by NCQA (the organization that owns HEDIS).
